definition: Representing more features than there are dimensions by assigning them to an overcomplete set of non-orthogonal directions, which is viable only when features activate sparsely -- the hypothesis that explains why individual neurons are polysemantic and why a learned dictionary is needed to recover features at all. Across 11 sources it is the premise the archive's interpretability work rests on rather than a claim it tests, and the corpus's contribution is mostly about what follows from it. If features are in superposition then no privileged basis exists, so a decomposition depends on the procedure that produced it -- which is the identifiability problem the sparse-autoencoder entry records empirically, with different seeds and widths recovering materially different features from the same activations. One source in the corpus questions whether the latent-thinking phenomena attributed to it are superposition at all, finding continuous and discrete decoding functionally indistinguishable on off-the-shelf models.

evidence.note: Compares two training-free intent classifiers built from summary statistics of prefill-time activations against trained heads on the same features, and finds the trade-off is not accuracy but where each fails — trained heads win fine-grained distinctions, statistical ones give better uncertainty on mixed prompts and survive adversarial rephrasing that collapses the trained heads to zero.
evidence.title: Training-Free versus Training-Based Intent Classification in LLMs: Accuracy, Robustness, and Failure Modes

evidence.note: Proves that activation patching and weight-space ablation measure two different quantities — a carrier's donor-receiver contrast versus its absolute level at the receiver — which neither bounds, gives an exact if-and-only-if criterion for when ablating a subset collapses a conditional onto one branch, and then withdraws its own clean empirical separation when it fails out of sample.
evidence.title: A Theory of Conditional Collapse under Low-Rank Weight-Space Ablations: I. The Single-Block Theory and Synthetic Validation

evidence.note: Extends a single-block interaction theorem to ablated subsets spanning many layers, isolates the cross-layer remainder as an exact double integral rather than bounding it, supplies the one missing closed-form ingredient (a local attention Jacobian bound, verified without a violation on a real 1.5B model), and tests the whole picture on an emergent circuit nobody designed for it — reporting the mixed outcome as mixed.
evidence.title: Cross-Layer Interaction under Weight-Space Ablation: A Closed-Form Attention Jacobian Bound and a Test on a Real Pretrained Model

evidence.note: Builds multi-layer steering vectors from SAE features selected by co-activation and decoder-direction alignment, and intervenes at several points instead of one.
evidence.title: CircuitSteer: Geometrically Aligned Multi-Layer Steering via Sparse Autoencoder Circuits

evidence.note: Shows that the part of a steering vector which breaks a model's refusal behaviour is a separate direction from the part that produces the intended behavioural effect, and learns that direction by constrained optimization so it can be ablated without losing the steering.
evidence.title: Safety Cost of Steering Vectors Is Separable and Reducible

evidence.note: Takes the set of active sparse-autoencoder latents as the unit of analysis and finds that adding a semantically compatible adjective to a noun deactivates 20 to 60 percent of the latents the noun alone had active, which contradicts the bag-of-features reading those sets are usually given.
evidence.title: Beyond a Bag of Features: Set-Level Instability in Sparse Autoencoders

evidence.note: Generalizes causal tracing from one component or layer at a time to selecting subsets of components jointly, by relaxing the combinatorial search into a continuous one over soft interventions.
evidence.title: Multi-component Causal Tracing in Large Language Models

evidence.note: Reads reasoning validity from layer-to-layer displacement of hidden states rather than from the states themselves, on the grounds that static activations let probes latch onto lexical surface patterns.
evidence.title: Truth as a Trajectory: What Internal Representations Reveal About Large Language Model Reasoning

evidence.note: Argues run-to-run feature consistency should be a standard SAE evaluation axis alongside reconstruction and sparsity, and gives a metric showing high consistency is achievable.
evidence.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Should Prioritize Feature Consistency in Sparse Autoencoders

evidence.note: Trains a sparse autoencoder over whole reasoning steps rather than tokens, conditioning both encoder and decoder on the preceding trajectory so the sparse code carries only what the step adds, and shows that step correctness, logicality, length and first token are all linearly decodable from that code.
evidence.title: Step-Level Sparse Autoencoder for Reasoning Process Interpretation

evidence.note: Trains sparse autoencoders on language model activations to recover an overcomplete dictionary of sparsely activating directions, and shows those directions are more interpretable and more precisely causal than neurons, PCA or ICA.
evidence.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models

name: superposition
